title: Supercommunicators: How to Unlock the Secret Language of Connection

contents: The three conversational modes: practical (What's this really about?), emotional (How do we feel?), social (Who are we?)
The matching principle: connection requires recognising and joining the conversation actually happening
Learning conversations and the techniques: looping for understanding, deep questions, proving you are listening
Emotional conversations: vulnerability, reciprocity, and the laughter studies
Identity conversations: who-are-we discussions, hard talks about race and belonging at Netflix
Applied cases: Jim Lawler's CIA recruitment of 'Yasmin', the Leroy Reed jury, The Big Bang Theory, vaccine conversations, gun-control dialogues
Online communication: politeness, hedges, gratitude, and not criticising in public

audiences: Managers and team leads who run hard conversations
Couples and families with recurring conversational stalemates
Negotiators, doctors, and anyone who must connect across disagreement
Readers of Duhigg's earlier behavioural books

sources.title: Supercommunicators by Charles Duhigg
sources.supports: Edition facts (Random House, 2024-02-20 hardcover; 2025-09-30 paperback, ISBN 9780593243923, 320pp), the three-conversations framework, the matching principle, and the headline case studies: CIA recruitment, jury deliberation, surgeon and patients, The Big Bang Theory writers' room.

sources.title: Supercommunicators (edition record)
sources.supports: Hardcover bibliographic record: Random House, 2024, ISBN 9780593243916.

sources.title: Supercommunicators (review)
sources.supports: A professional trade review: praises the three-conversations framework, the empathetic-listening starting point, and the practical focus; verdict that Duhigg 'unpacks the essential tools for effective, positive conversations'; no star.

sources.title: Supercommunicators by Charles Duhigg (review)
sources.author_or_publisher: Ayesha Anna Ninan, Stanford Social Innovation Review
sources.supports: An independent critical review: the advice is 'rather obvious', the framework lacks groundbreaking insight, ethics of persuasive skill go unexamined, online-discourse advice is simplistic about harassment, and the tools thin out at societal scale.

sources.title: Supercommunicators — Book Review
sources.supports: Detailed content walkthrough: looping for understanding, deep questions that convert facts to values, the four online rules (politeness, less sarcasm, more gratitude and hedges, no public criticism), and the case-study roster including Netflix, NASA, gun-control dialogues, and vaccine conversations.
sources.limitations: Blog review; used for content structure, with a faith-based editorial slant on some judgements.

sources.title: Supercommunicators: The Power of Connection
sources.supports: The author's own framing: three conversations, the matching principle, and 'with the right tools, we can connect with anyone'.

sources.title: Supercommunicators: How to Unlock the Secret Language of Connection
sources.supports: Large, broadly positive reader reception; recurring notes that the material overlaps active-listening classics and that stories pad the framework.

sources.title: Supercommunicators Prologue Summary & Analysis
sources.supports: Prologue detail: FBI negotiator Felix Sigala as the opening case (including the barricaded man with a room full of snakes), and the framing of supercommunicators as ordinary people running learnable procedures.
sources.limitations: Study-guide summary, not the text itself.

sources.title: A Guide for Teachers and Students: Supercommunicators
sources.supports: Official companion confirming the book's structure, the named cases (Jim Lawler's CIA recruitment of 'Yasmin', the jury, The Big Bang Theory writers' room, Netflix), and the learning-conversation techniques.

sources.title: Hyperscanning: A Valid Method to Study Neural Inter-brain Underpinnings of Social Interaction
sources.author_or_publisher: D. Czeszumski and colleagues; Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
sources.supports: Independent review of inter-brain synchrony methods: the field is young and mainly exploratory; shared stimuli, varied measures, speech artefacts, small samples, and mixed frequency findings limit simple interpretations.
sources.limitations: Methodological review of hyperscanning generally, not a direct review of Duhigg's wording or every study used in the book.

workflow.coverage_notes: Secondary coverage via two independent professional reviews, the publisher's official companion materials, and detailed chapter summaries including the documented prologue; no full-text read.
